An early own goal put Celtic in front but they were soon pegged back after failing to clear their lines twice and they left it late to make their second-half possession count.

Kasper Hogh started up front in place of Duran but went a 17th Celtic game without scoring before the former Qarabag striker came on and netted his 15th goal of the season.

Two of those goals came off the bench against Besiktas last time out in the Europa League when he helped inspire a comeback victory.

O’Neill told Celtic Player: “In the game against Besiktas, he was substitute and we had a particular plan that evening “Here we have to try and win the game, but also sometimes you have to gamble a little bit as well too. Kasper starts at centre-forward.

“Of course, by the time that Camilo comes on, the game might be beyond you. But you feel when he’s on the field that something’s going to happen for us and that’s the sign of a brilliant player.”

Jota’s cross led to the opening goal and the Portuguese winger was Celtic’s brightest player before going off just before the hour mark on his first European appearance since the Hoops came within seconds of beating Bayern Munich in Germany in February 2025.

“He did superbly well,” O’Neill said. “He’s getting fitter each game he plays. That’s the longest he’s lasted so far and he did really well.

“Obviously, on Portuguese soil, he’ll want to do well. But remember, he’s been out of the game for about 18, 19, 20 months. It’s a long, long time to try and get that sort of max fitness again, but he’s improving each game.”

Forrest drew level with Scott Brown’s Celtic record of 127 European appearances.

“It’s not just that, he’s making an impact,” O’Neill said of the 35-year-old. “When he comes on, there’s something going to happen. He’s got that fantastic burst of speed that I honestly don’t think he’ll lose when he’s 50. A great club man as well and he’s got a big heart.”

Celtic lost their opening three European games but have resurrected their hopes of progression ahead of next month’s trip to face Omonia Nicosia in Cyprus.

“I think people started to get carried away because this was a Portuguese second division side,” O’Neill said. “They were that in name only. They’ve got some really fine players who could definitely play much, much higher.

“To give ourselves six points, we give ourselves a chance.”

#1881. I watched Celtic leave it late in Portugal and noted gamble pay off, emotional homecoming and serious issue

Unconvincing Celtic kept their Europa League qualification hopes alive with a hard-fought and historic 2-1 victory over Portuguese second-tier side Torreense.

Martin O’Neill’s men took an early lead through a Javi Vazquez own goal after nine minutes, but Dany Jean restored parity for the hosts before half-time in Leiria.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The visitors struggled to find a breakthrough after the interval, until substitute Camilo Duran rose unmarked to head home James Forrest’s cross in the 84th minute.

The late winner secured a second consecutive victory in the competition for Celtic, moving them on to six points from five matches and up to 25th in the league-phase standings after keeping their hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

It was also the Scottish champions’ victory win on Portuguese soil since 2003.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold for The Scotsman and picks out his four main takeaways from the game.

Celtic may have made unnecessarily hard work of beating a Portuguese second division outfit currently sitting 13th in their league, but Martin O’Neill will care little about the aesthetics after securing three precious points.

Although Celtic enjoyed plenty of possession after the interval, their use of the ball was frequently pedestrian, with too many passes going sideways or backwards rather than putting Torreense under meaningful pressure. There were spells when Celtic appeared destined to settle for a frustrating draw, but ultimately they have given themselves a genuine opportunity to reach the play-off round and, at this stage of their European campaign, that is what matters most.

Once again, Camilo Duran proved to be the difference-maker. O’Neill's decision to keep the in-form striker in reserve paid dividends, with the substitute delivering the decisive moment when Celtic needed a spark. The Colombian’s back-post header from fellow replacement James Forrest’s pinpoint delivery was precisely the injection of quality that had been missing for much of the evening.

When the ball arrived at his feet, his first touch was outstanding, allowing him to open his body and switch the play. He then demonstrated the instincts of a natural goal scorer, occupying defenders before finding the space to deliver the decisive finish. Duran may have had only 12 touches, but the one that mattered most was emphatic. He is becoming Celtic's go-to man in crucial moments, and delivered once more when it counted.

Although Jota did not manage to get his name on the scoresheet or provide an assist, his performance in Portugal offered plenty of telltale signs that he is rediscovering the devastating form that once made him such an exciting attacking presence for Celtic. The winger looked particularly at home on his return to familiar surroundings, relishing the chance to perform in front of friends and family after an arduous period on the sidelines.

Making his first European appearance since Celtic’s Champions League disappointment against Bayern Munich in February 2025, the 27-year-old showed few signs of rustiness despite two injury-disrupted seasons. He was a constant menace to Torreense down the left flank, using his pace, close control and willingness to take on defenders to cause problems throughout his time on the pitch.

His influence was particularly evident during the opening period, creating two opportunities, testing the goalkeeper twice and delivering a succession of enticing crosses that deserved more decisive finishing from his team-mates. One such delivery contributed to Celtic's opening goal, when Vazquez inadvertently turned the ball into his own net.

Given the length of his absence and the physical demands of returning to elite-level football, there had been understandable questions over whether Jota could recapture the explosive qualities that previously made him a favourite among the Celtic support. His latest display provided a really encouraging response. There is still work to do before he reaches his previous heights, but the signs are increasingly promising.

This success has breathed fresh life into Celtic's European campaign, but O’Neill will be under no illusions that there is considerable scope for improvement if his side are to make further progress. Individual contributions may have rescued the evening in Portugal, yet they should not disguise some worrying collective shortcomings, particularly the vulnerability of the defence and the lack of composure when chances presented themselves in the final third.

The format offers Celtic a route into the knockout stages, with the top eight in the league phase advancing automatically to the last 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th must negotiate a two-legged play-off. There remains little margin for error, though, with three fixtures remaining. Celtic still have Omonoia, Marseille and current league-phase leaders Union Saint-Gilloise to negotiate, and will almost certainly require further points if they are to extend their European journey.

There is, however, reason for optimism. The win over Torreense means Celtic have now recorded successive wins in a major European competition for the first time since defeating Ferencvaros home and away during the 2021-22 group stage of this tournament. It is a positive milestone for O’Neill's side and another indication that, despite their problems, Celtic are beginning to build some momentum at a crucial stage.

Torreense may have been unfancied on paper, but they demonstrated they were no pushovers and gave Celtic a considerably sterner test than their second-tier status might have suggested. The Portuguese outfit were organised, and disciplined, refusing to be overawed by the occasion or the gulf in resources between the two clubs.

João Nuno’s side pressed aggressively, competed well for second balls and showed enough attacking ambition to expose some of Celtic's defensive vulnerabilities. Their equaliser was reward for an approach that refused to crumble after falling behind, while their resistance after the interval threatened to frustrate the visitors further.

Celtic's superior individual quality eventually told, but Torreense deserve credit for making them dig deep for the result. This was no routine European assignment. For all the criticism Celtic will face over aspects of their performance, Torreense should not be dismissed as cannon fodder. They showed spirit and sufficient quality to suggest their lowly league position told only part of the story.

#1878. ‘Curious’ Derek McInnes used Jamestown Analytics to rate Rangers signing while Hearts manager

Derek McInnes has revealed that he used Jamestown Analytics to rate Rangers' signing of Ryan Naderi while manager of Hearts last season.

Hearts gained access to Jamestown's treasure trove of player recruitment data in 2024 after selling a stake in the club to the man who formed the company, Brighton chairman Tony Bloom.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While used primarily to source signings for their own squad, Hearts are also able to access information on signings made by their Premiership rivals.

McInnes admitted that he ran Naderi through the system and was left hoping that Rangers would not sign the Czech striker as he was identified as a good signing for the Ibrox club.

He explained: "Last January, obviously, when we first seen that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everyone else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'How do they rate him?'

"Because you're always curious. It's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated. That's the way it was. It's just natural.

"But no, he was someone that I think was well known to them. I think Brugge had an interest in Ryan, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well. But the kind of money, the fee, it just kind of went away for them, I think.

"But we were told that he was a good player before I'd even set eyes on him. The feeling was that he was somebody that could help Rangers and make them better. So when I'd seen a lot of the comings and goings, it was on, it was off, it was off, on again, I was kind of hoping that it would fall through, being the Hearts manager. But when I'd seen they'd signed him, I knew that Rangers had strengthened. And I think Rangers did strengthen well in January last year.

"So that was the first we kind of looked a wee bit more at him but, again, you just do it as an opposition manager, looking at him. It's only when you get to work with people on a daily basis that you get to see them."

Naderi initially struggled to live up to his £4.75million transfer tag after joining Rangers in January from German third tier side Hansa Rostock.

However, the 23-year-old has emerged as a talismanic figure this season, scoring 10 goals in his last 20 games and providing the focal point in attack following injuries to Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland.

"I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door about what we felt this season could look like for him," McInnes said. "Because it's not always easy for a young player settling in January and they're in the middle of a race, but to try and really establish himself this season.

"I think he stood up brilliantly to a couple of the senior injuries, to other injuries throughout, to Youssef and Lawrence. He's had to be the guy and he's led the line brilliantly. I love the goals he scores. I love his work rate anyway. But it's nice that people don't just see him as a grafter now and a worker. He's actually got good intelligence.

"All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time and it's symptomatic of some of the goals he scores, following things in, just always believing there might just be something there for me.

"I love having a striker that has the ability to score those types of goals. But he leads the line well, gets us up the pitch and works ever so hard, as you know. He's done well. He should feel pleased. I think the fact that he's got capped as well, he's taken a real step on from that. I think he's taken a lot of confidence from that.

"However he gets his confidence, whether it's scoring goals, whether it's staying fit, being a big part of the team, whether it's getting recognised at international level, we all want it to continue."

Dolan dissected the week’s events with us and said: “You’d have to say Broadbridge Heath deserved the win. First half, I don’t think they caused us too many problems. Momentum is important – like when you’re doing well and a goal goes in against you, which was an unfortunate error from Harry (Haines). It just went under his hand – there wasn’t much power in it from 20 yards.

"I’m not going to hold that against Harry, he’s been good for us this season. But when things aren’t going for you, little things like that go against you. It kills the momentum you had in the game and it does knock the stuffing out of people a bit.

"You’ve just got to stay on it and that’s what we’re doing with the boys in training – back to basics, try to keep things simple, don’t over-complicate things, try to make the right decisions, get in the right areas. We’re working hard on putting it right.

"Our boys are prepared for that, we’ve been going through it in training.

"Elliott coming in is great competition for the frontline boys. He can play anywhere acorss the frontline and knows the level really well. He’s very good with the ball at his feet and knows where the goal is. He’ll get firing for us.

"He came in for his debut (at Heath) not really knowing any of the boys and will need a game or two to get up to speed with how we play."

Of Chapman’s switch to league rivals Margate, Dolan said: "Mitch has moved on. We have had three approaches for him in the time we have had him, from step three and step four, and this one was in line with where he lives and where they train.

"Mitch did a great job for us – he filled in for me when I was injured – but players move and I have a lot of time for Mitch and have no issue with him moving on.

"We’re hoping to have another one or two added to the squad ready for Saturday. Hopefully we can get them over the line and move on and get the win Saturday.”

Hastingsknow a visit to Punjab United will not be easy. Dolan said: “It will be a hard game away from home. I’ve played there and their pitch is on a bit of a slope. "They’re a very big, physical, direct side, from what I know.”

#1875. Man United must build on improved Sporting Lisbon display in vital Premier League clash with Brentford

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:51, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:55

Manchester United will continue their Premier League campaign against Brentford on Saturday afternoon, and Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law has discussed all of the latest talking points surrounding the 20-time English champions.

Man United conceded the most goals, 36, the most penalties, five, and the most red cards, five, of any Premier League team this season.

The Liverpool game was controversial as well, with the red card for Leny Yoro that has since been rescinded. Isak does not have even a little bit of control of the ball. He has ballooned it 10 metres in front of him, and still, he is given the red card for that one.

That was a huge turning moment in the game. That is not to say that United should be going on and losing 4-0 at Anfield, even with 10 men, but it is a game-changing incident.

It leaves United on one Premier League win this season, down in 19th spot in the table, eight points from 11 games, which is absolutely horrendous. What I would say is it was a tough start for Pochettino. It was a big game at Anfield against the Liverpool side that played well.

If you concede that red card and then the fact they score from the free kick, that is a real hammer blow, and then you have to hold on and try to keep it 1-0 going into the second half.

United could not do that. The performance level was well off it again. They conceded four goals in each of their last two Premier League games. It is 23 goals conceded now in the Premier League in 11 games.

This team just cannot keep clean sheets for love nor money, in the Premier League, in any competition. Not kept a clean sheet since the win over Sabah in the Champions League, their first Champions League game in the league phase.

If you keep a clean sheet, you have got a really good chance of winning football games. If you concede two a game, three a game, you are just not going to pick up wins.

The game against Sporting Lisbon was one we could do a two-hour podcast on. The first penalty against Sporting is very soft.

If that is a penalty then we might as well pack up and do podcasts on something else, because I do not want to be a part of a game that says that is a penalty. The Senne Lammens one is a penalty. What is he doing? He is flying out.

Then the goal that was disallowed for Amad, how that is a foul from Tielemans I will never know. An absolute horrific decision. The Fernandes penalty is a penalty for me.

I think it is a straightforward decision. I do not think it is a foul on Senne Lammens, and I also do not think it is a foul for the last goal.

Dorgu got penalised for jumping into the goalkeeper, but they are either both fouls or neither are fouls. The contact on Senne Lammens for the Sporting equaliser was soft. I do not think that should be disallowed.

I do not think the United goal should be disallowed. The late red card was clumsy from Tielemans. It is not vintage football, it is not vintage Man United. They struggled in the final third of the field. Zirkzee came into the side and did okay.

An interesting stat from that game was that United had 12 high turnovers against Sporting, their most in any game this season.

It did feel like they were winning the ball back higher. They were definitely pressing more as a unit. The shape of the team was better. They need a centre forward. If they had had Sesko last night and that threat in behind, you feel like they could have picked up all three points.

They were decent on the ball, recovered well from going behind in the game. Sporting are a good side and have had good results in the Champions League this season.

They are a really strong team with really good players. There were positives from the Sporting Lisbon game, and it leaves them in a decent enough position in the Champions League.

They need to beat Leipzig in the next European game if they are really going to push on. They have got Bayern Munich and Villarreal as well, and those are going to be difficult games.

From the Champions League point of view, I still think they are in a decent enough position to finish in, whether that is the automatic qualification places or ultimately the play-offs.

Dealing with the Premier League is where they need to focus. They have got three games in a row now before the Leipzig game: Brentford, Newcastle away, Coventry at home.

The next two home games are absolutely massive. If they get turned over here and then go to Newcastle and do not manage to get a win, and then Coventry pick something up against them, it is very difficult.

I do not think United are getting relegated this season. I say that out of hope. I think they are going to be busy in January. They are going to have to be inventive.

Around £50m is the figure they are going to have to spend. They need to bring in three players: definitely a striker, definitely a centre-back, definitely a full-back.

Carlos Baleba is going to be back sooner than expected. They are going to hope to get Rashford back at some stage in the not-too-distant future. Those two did train in the gym ahead of the Sporting game. Shaw was back on the bench as well.

Pochettino said he was proud of his players for their performance level in the Sporting game and for overcoming the adversity, because there were some really horrific decisions from the referee and VAR in that game.

United have not had the rub of the green. With the Fernandes goal and the divot, they showed the earlier clip and it was Fernandes himself who had made that divot in the turf.

He had had a heavy touch with his boot in the box, and they circled back and it was the one he had made. So he actually managed to assist himself with that bobble. There has been a lot that has gone against United this season.

This is a really big game on Saturday afternoon and one I am hoping they can win against Brentford. First Premier League win for Pochettino. Go to the Newcastle game, can you get a point? Can you go there and beat Coventry? Can you beat Leipzig? Football changes very quickly. If you put three or four good results together, everyone feels different.

It goes in cycles. A big football match. Brentford, it is one of those games that back in the day, United at home to Brentford, you would think it is a gimme, a home win.

But they are an excellent team, Brentford, sitting sixth in the table at the moment with 17 points. Going away from home brings its different challenges, and without Igor Thiago as well is a big one.

I did also want to mention Senne Lammens' form, which is a concern for me.

Going back to the middle of September, Paul Scholes said in a podcast, The Good, The Bad and the Football, that he questioned whether Lammens was good enough, at a stage when he was actually playing quite well.

And I have to be honest, I am in that camp now. He is making a lot of mistakes.

There was one in the Sporting game last night where they did not concede from it, but he pushed the ball back into the middle and no one was on the rebound to put it away. The mistake for the second goal was a big one as well.

His form is slightly concerning and his confidence looks shot at the moment. I think he starts here, but it will be interesting to see whether United ultimately think they might have to get another goalkeeper in at some stage.

#1871. GdS: ‘Numbers like Kaka’ – why Rabiot is so important to Milan with renewal imminent

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this new era.

The former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

With five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim said after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

#1869. Celtic defend head of security amid fan group tensions

Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared that four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A statement from the ultras group stated the four had been “finally cleared of wrongdoing” over the incident, which took place during a game against Falkirk on October 25 last year.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The group accused Celtic of “smearing” them with their statement on November 7 last year, which outlined an indefinite ban on about 250 supporters that eventually lasted nearly six months.

Celtic had written that about 100 Green Brigade members took part in an “orchestrated” attempt to prevent an individual being arrested following an incident with a steward and that the large group “verbally abused and assaulted the steward and police officers”.

A Green Brigade statement read: “Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

“The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed.”

The group called for Celtic to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with the club’s head of security, Mark Hargreaves, at last year’s abandoned annual general meeting.

“This week’s outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year,” they added.

“It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves’ subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives.

“We maintain that Mark Hargreaves has introduced a poisonous security culture to Celtic Park and does not hold the trust of supporters whose safety he is supposed to be responsible for. His position is untenable.”

Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

A statement added: “The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

“Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council.”

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a “campaign of personal harassment and abuse” towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

They added: “Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

“Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action.”

#1866. Why Barnsley FC captain Cameron McGeehan has sympathy for Daniel Stendel amid wretched League One run

Both are in their second spells at the club and the former had his best year at Oakwell during the German's memorable first season as head coach in 2018-19.

Given what the Reds are currently experiencing, that magnificent promotion campaign must seem like a world away.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The pair are now fighting fires at the wrong end of League One; beleaguered Barnsley currently prop up the table following a wretched 11-match winless streak.

In his second coming at Oakwell, Stendel named McGeehan, a player he rates and trusts, as his on-pitch leader in the summer.

So far this term, the Reds chief has largely been spared the ire of increasingly agitated followers; most have elected to vent their frustration toward the Oakwell hierarchy instead.

But given Barnsley's atrocious autumnal numbers - two points taken from the last available 33 - chatter is also starting to centre on the German's position.

For McGeehan, the club's top-scorer with nine goals, it provides a personal element in his quest to help the stricken Reds change the narrative of a hard season.

He also shares sympathy with Stendel, given Barnsley's tendencies to continually shoot themselves in the foot - which he feels has nothing to do with the head coach.

A case in point was at Bradford City on Tuesday, when all three of the visitors' concessions were self-inflicted.

Speaking ahead of the crunch trip to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, McGeehan said: "I think coming in after the game, a lot of the boys were saying: 'the gaffer's going to be pulling his hair out' because that was just down to the players' mistakes.

"And it's happened too many times this season, we've made poor individual errors that have led to goals and caused us to lose games we probably shouldn't have.

"We want to get a positive result for everyone at the club.

"But obviously the gaffer's someone I've worked with before and you can see it completely consumes him. He wants the very best and he's passionate to get Barnsley into a good place, as we all are. We're all fighting together.

"It can all change very quickly. But it starts with us on the pitch getting a positive result. This poor run's lasted way too long and we've got to draw a line in the sand.

"Obviously, there's a lot of positive things that we've done in games and it's just trying to get that game where it clicks and then you go from there."

The busy run to the turn of the year looks critical for Barnsley, currently four points adrift of safety, with several fixtures coming up against sides around them.

Should the Reds manage to chip away with some much-needed wins, January will come into sharp focus.

Recruiting a defensive lieutenant and an experienced leader of the line are surely two huge priorities for a side that is currently dangerously weak in both boxes, where games are decided, despite getting other things right elsewhere.

On the importance of bringing in some seniority in the new year at the sharp ends of the pitch, McGeehan observed: "Potentially. You can look at that obviously when you're not doing well, you sort of start to pick apart different things.

"At the start of the season, when we started quite well, you sort of think: 'oh, we've got a youthful, energetic side'.

"There's always two ways you can spin it. I've seen experienced players make mistakes for goals and be short of confidence as well. January will come and teams always make signings but all we are concentrating on is now and do what we can with what we've got.

"We've got some really good players here and hopefully we can turn the corner. It's everyone sticking together and trying to fight. It's the only way out of this."

McGeehan admits that listening to opposing managers and pundits continuing to label Barnsley as a good footballing side is becoming 'boring'.

For his part, Stendel concurs, adding: "This is easy to say when you win the game and keep the points. I don't like it."

The Reds boss also has no truck with the disquiet of supporters either.

It spilled over at the final whistle at Valley Parade on Tuesday with chants of 'You're not fit to wear the shirt' aimed at players.

The Oakwell boss, who confirmed that Reyes Cleary is not yet back in training, with Cieran Slicker and Makenzie Kirk having issues ahead of the weekend, added: "When you are upset, you say things like that. This is not different at Barnsley to other clubs in the world.

"I also have to support and protect my team. They are trying to do their best. It is not enough at the moment for the expectation of what we have as a club and also not for the supporters."

As for what happens next, Winterton isinterim manager and the Town committee have asked fans to get behind him as he guides the squad through what will be a tricky period.

Those won’t be easy games with a number of Macdonald’s players announcing they also left – including James Waters, who had only rejoined the club a day before the manager was ousted.

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 20:17, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:19

Real Betis will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume domestic affairs at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday afternoon.

The Seville outfit lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 21 victories to Rayo's 13, while 16 of their 50 previous matches have finished all square.

Real Betis will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-0 win over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, with the result leaving them sixth in the overall table, claiming 12 points from their five games in the league stage of the tournament.

Manuel Pellegrini's side boast a record of eight wins, three draws and two defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 27 points leaving them in fourth spot in the La Liga table, five points ahead of fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

Real Betis are only four points behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, but they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sevilla in the Seville derby last weekend.

El Glorioso were last victorious in the league on November 8, beating Elche 2-0, while their last defeat at this level was a 5-2 home reverse to Barcelona on October 17.

Real Betis will be in Copa del Rey action against CD Extremadura on December 1 before facing Atletico Madrid in La Liga ahead of their next Champions League fixture with Como.

Rayo, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of successive defeats to Real Sociedad and Valencia in Spain's top flight, and it has been a tough season to date for the capital outfit.

Benat San Jose's side have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches to sit in 16th spot in the division on 12 points, level on points with 18th-placed Getafe.

Rayo have the third-worst away record in Spain's top flight this season, picking up just two points from six matches, which is a concern ahead of this game.

Los Franjirrojos have actually drawn their last four matches against Real Betis, while they have not been beaten by the Seville outfit since September 2023.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw in the corresponding game during the 2025-26 campaign, and it was also 1-1 when they locked horns in the same stadium in December 2024.

Real Betis remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension, while Dani Ceballos, Giovani Lo Celso, Iker Losada and Jose Morante are out through injury.

Cucho Hernandez scored twice against Slovan Bratislava on his return from injury on Tuesday evening, and the 27-year-old is now set to come in for his first league appearance since the middle of October.

Antony and Isco are both set to retain their spots in the final third of the field, while Pablo Fornals is likely to be joined by Marc Roca in the middle of the midfield.

As for Rayo, Augusto Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin are out through injury, but the capital outfit have no fresh fitness concerns.

Sergio Camello has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 13 appearances, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be another spot at centre-forward for Randy Nteka despite the fact that the 28-year-old is still waiting for his first goal of the campaign.

#1857. Moreirense vs Santa Clara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are currently some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary issues against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose issue.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

A Ferreira; Pinto, Kevyn Monteiro, Batista, A Martinez; N John, Liberato; Andrade, Mendonca, Landerson; Vonic

Franca; Lucas Soares, Ythallo, H Silva, Fofana; Tavares, Borges, Vasconcelos; V Lopes, Paciencia, B Lucas

Santa Clara have been considerably stronger away from home this season, but their defensive absences could prove costly against a Moreirense side that have won three of the last four meetings between the clubs.

Furthermore, the hosts have an opportunity to exploit an inexperienced centre-back pairing, although their own scoring problems and the visitors' impressive away record suggest neither side will have enough to claim all three points.

#1855. Silly Leeds United punishment shows Daniel Farke's serious approach to complacency

Earlier in the season, the German manager told The Yorkshire Post of his – slightly tongue in cheek – horror at Ao Tanaka wearing gloves in training before the weather had turned cold, and this week he gave a member of staff a dressing down to try and keep his squad grounded after Saturday's hugely impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea.

Both the "crime" and the punishment were light-hearted but with a serious message about complacency, and it is a balance Farke always looks to strike.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds are in seventh in the Premier League and have consistently been around the likely positions to qualify for Europe this season, but Farke has always taken a two-pronged attitude towards expectations, encouraging supporters to get ahead of themselves but not those who work for him.

"What I can guarantee is I will make sure that no one here at the training ground at Thorp Arch is too big time and I'm not one per cent concerned about my players," he said when the topic of Europe was raised ahead of Saturday's Premier League visit from newly-promoted Coventry City.

"We had a staff member this week who came out after a great win against Chelsea more or less celebrating in the first session.

"I know it's a bit colder right now and you have to put yourself into warm clothes but instead of wearing a hat (for training) – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head like a 20-year-old creative No 10 who enjoys himself.

"It was as if he had won the game at Chelsea all alone.

"It was a long working day for him, I made sure. He was treating our kit men and from now on he stays in shorts and T-shirts until the end of January on the outside pitches.

"I don't allow anyone to be big time, not one staff member, not one player. We know exactly what we're coming from and if anyone thinks we are too good for this and can be cool like a 20-year-old No 10, one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is back to work and doesn't enjoy himself too much.

"We have not achieved 38 points so far (his mark for avoiding relegation), so there's no reason to lean back, just enjoy and stop working.

"It's good to be already on 17 points at this stage (11 games in). It's definitely a good amount and gives us confidence and belief in what you're doing.

"But at this level the momentum can change quickly and for that we won't allow ourselves to be too big time or to enjoy ourselves too much.

"We are in a good mood at the moment and we work, train and play with confidence but nothing else.

"The Premier League is the best league in the world. We can only win points if we are 100 per cent on it."

A silly response to a seemingly trivial offence (with a much more serious underlying issue) is a balance Farke is conscious of striking.

"It's perhaps not typical for a German fella to have a good sense of humour – at least that's a bit the reputation – but I think in general everyone is at his best in every job when you feel valued, when you feel comfortable when you do your job with confidence and this is also what we try to create," commented Farke.

"I've seen some statistics that we were the hardest-working side over the last (Premier League) weekend. At Chelsea we covered more distance and high-speed intensity runs than any other team at Premier League level.

"This is one side of how we work really hard with focused, concentrated work but we always want to do this with a smile on our face.

"We want to make sure that everyone enjoys coming to work and it's not just hoping for the next day off so I don't see the manager, the staff member or assistant coach.

"Sometimes you have to give them a day off but we also want to create an atmosphere where everyone feels safe and is allowed to make a joke and also joke at my costs.

"You also give the sign that you know how important and how serious football is but it's never more important than the human being.

"When I name the squad on Friday there are some tough decisions and top players won't make it. When I name the starting line-up it's tough for them but then we have to make sure that we have something to cheer and to laugh about.

"Hopefully the most important thing is success and winning points but also to have a good atmosphere.

"I hope my jokes are not too old-school for the players because I'm getting older and older."

Meanwhile, striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract until the end of 2028-29, by when he will have just turned 32.

"I want to keep my best players without giving them the scenario that they can lean back because they've signed a ten-year deal," said his manager. "I've made it clear (to the board) but it was easy because everyone in our hierarchy wants to keep the best players."

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s new manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

“In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” said the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

“You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he said.

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

But when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their big spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

‘I think at the very beginning he showed why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips said when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a big game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’

Pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:49

Coming off a three-week break from competitive action, Academico de Viseu and Alverca meet at Estadio do Fontelo on Saturday evening in what will be their first-ever encounter in Portugal's top flight.

The hosts occupy sixth place in the Primeira Liga table, eight points and five positions ahead of their visitors, who are four points above the relegation play-off spot.

Academico de Viseu have made an encouraging return to the top flight after a 37-year absence, having collected six wins from their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L3), scoring 15 times and conceding 13 at the other end.

Bruno Pinheiro's side, who failed to record a victory in any of their first four outings this term, enjoyed a particularly impressive spell between September 6 and November 1, winning six consecutive league matches, including a famous triumph away to Sporting Lisbon on October 25.

However, that winning run in the top flight came to an end last time out, when the Viseu club suffered a 1-0 defeat to Nacional in Funchal after conceding a late winner to Matchoi Djalo.

The result also means Academico have now alternated between defeats and victories across their last five matches in all competitions, including cup losses to lower-division Fatima in the Taca de Portugal and Primeira Liga champions Porto in the Taca da Liga.

Returning from a three-week hiatus, the Viseu club will be glad to be back at Fontelo, where they have won each of their last three matches, beating Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estoril Praia and Rio Ave by 2-1 scorelines after losing their opening two fixtures at the ground this term.

Like the hosts, Alverca also started the campaign slowly, failing to record a victory in any of their opening five fixtures, but enjoyed a three-match winning run between September 12 and October 12, beating Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao.

However, the Ribatejo club have slipped back into familiar struggles, having since gone winless in four matches across all competitions, starting with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of second-tier Tondela before suffering narrow league defeats against Arouca and Benfica.

Sergio Ferreira's team then drew 1-1 with Casa Pia in their most recent outing, with Ian Luccas finding the net in the 66th minute to rescue a point, while the goal ended a three-match run without scoring.

Two wins from their last three league games on the road suggest Alverca have also held their own away from home, although they have been vulnerable when not at their best, losing three of their five away league outings this season.

There is also little to draw from history, given the Ribatejo club are without a victory in their previous three meetings with Academico, losing twice in that spell, although their most recent visit to Viseu ended in a 2-2 draw in February 2025 in Liga 2.

Academico de Viseu form (all competitions):

With no reported injury or suspension concerns, Academico head coach Pinheiro could retain a similar lineup to the one that featured against Nacional, with goalkeeper Ewerton shielded by the defensive quartet of Anthony Correia, Nikolaos Michelis, Robinho and Miguel Angel Brau.

Andre Clovis has scored five of the Viseu club's 15 league goals this season and also provided an assist, with the Brazilian expected to lead the line here.

Alverca could be without Rayan Lucas, who remains a doubt after suffering another setback with his left knee, although the midfielder has returned to integrated training.

Nabil Touaizi is also expected to miss out after suffering a relapse of a right-calf injury, while Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai remain sidelined following knee surgery.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Noah Raveyre is another absentee, with his return expected in early December.

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Guilherme, Kahraman, Mortimer; Clovis

Mendes; Boyan, Gomez, James; Spencer, I Luccas, Gui, Chissumba; Chiquinho, Camara, Figueiredo

Academico have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, but their overall league form and stronger position in the table make them worthy favourites against an Alverca side that have scored just once in their last four matches, so a home victory looks plausible.

#1849. Brighton v Newcastle: Fabian Hurzeler delivers honest verdict on Ibrahim Osman after two-goal blast

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler has urged Ibrahim Osman to remain patient but be “ready and alive” as he waits for an opportunity to establish himself in the Premier League after starring in Europe.

Winger Osman scored twice – his first goals for the Seagulls – and also provided an assist in Thursday evening’s 4-0 Conference League win over Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The 21-year-old has been limited to 41 minutes of top-flight action across four substitute appearances this season after being loaned to Feyenoord, Auxerre and Birmingham since his 2024 arrival from Danish club Nordsjaelland.

“It’s not always the fact that he has to do more; sometimes the players who are currently on the pitch do a lot to stay on the pitch,” said Hurzeler.

“Therefore he needs to keep working hard, he needs to be patient, he needs to be there when we need him.

“We have plenty of games in the next weeks and I always emphasise that we need the full squad, that we need everyone, everyone will play an important role for us.

“No matter how many minutes you play, you need to contribute to the success for this club and we need to always put the team first. Some players might have to be a little bit more patient but in the right moment you need to be there so you have to always be ready and alive to support the team.”

Brighton, who sit second in the Premier League, will look to bounce back from last weekend’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull when they host Newcastle on Sunday.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is open to a return to Sporting CP before his career ends.

Fernandes spent three years in the Portuguese capital before joining United in January 2020. Th attacking midfielder has been the club’s best signing of the post Sir Alex Ferguson era but his future at Old Trafford is in more doubt than ever amid the club’s worst season in 40 years.

The Portugal international has already rejected to new contract offers. His current deal is set to expire in the summer but United do have the option to extend that by a further 12 months.

Fernandes is back at his old club this week with United taking on Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night. Speaking on Tuesday, the skipper revealed talks over a new deal are on hold now but was also quizzed on his club future.

Al-Hilal have made repeated attempts to sign the attacking midfielder but Fernandes says he would consider a return to Sporting if the chance were to present itself.

#1846. GdS: Amorim to field strong side vs. Olympiacos in bid to fix Europa League struggles

AC Milan will head to Greece on Thursday with the need to overturn a negative trend, so Ruben Amorim will leave nothing to chance.

In the past few weeks (barring the international break), Milan have alternated good performances at weekends with disastrous midweek results. The collapse against Bologna is one example, while losses to Bournemouth and Ferencvaros have complicated the Europa League mission.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Amorim won’t be opting for the usual excessive rotation against Olympiacos on Thursday night in Athens. There will be some changes, but the coach will field several regular starters.

The paper report that Amorim knows full well that victory is the only acceptable result in order for the Rossoneri to get back on track in their big to qualify for at least the Europa League play-offs, with the top eight now a distant mirage.

The Portuguese will rest Luka Modric in midfield. He will be replaced by Ardon Jashari, who scored his first goal for the Rossoneri in the win over Genoa. Adrien Rabiot – the Rossoneri’s driving force in this first part of the season – will remain in the team.

Up front, the same attack that played against Frosinone should be seen, namely Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira supporting Gonçalo Ramos, who finally returned to scoring after more than a month without a goal.

Both Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchison are raring to go, but both are expected to start on the bench in Athens, ready to come on as substitutes. Beyond the players, it will be crucial for Milan to take to the pitch with the right attitude.

#1845. Brighton’s Conference League qualification path explained - How many points are needed after Craiova win?

Brighton still require six more points to guarantee their place in the last 16 of the Uefa Conference League following Thursday night's impressive 4-0 victory over Romanian league leaders Craiova.

Fabian Hurzeler's side are currently second in the league phase table - behind leaders Monaco - with 10 points from their opening four matches, putting them in a strong position to secure automatic qualification for the knockout stages.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The top eight teams qualify directly for the last 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th must negotiate an additional knockout play-off round.

Brighton have two league-phase fixtures remaining, starting with a home meeting against leaders Monaco on December 10 before travelling to face Panathinaikos on December 17.

Winning both matches would take the Seagulls to 16 points and guarantee a top-eight finish, regardless of results elsewhere.

Four points from the remaining games would leave them on 14 and extremely well placed, although mathematical qualification would not be certain.

Three points would see them to 13 points and would still have a strong chance, depending on other results.

Hurzeler will be particularly encouraged by Brighton's defensive record, with the Seagulls yet to concede a goal in their four Conference League matches.

The Albion have scored nine times and will now look to finish the league phase strongly and avoid the extra play-off round in February.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler was delighted with the performance against Craiova

The German said: “I think that was a really good start, and also very important to make the game look easy, because especially the first goal helped us force [the opponent] to open up the space,” he said.

“That meant we could have more space to combine and more opportunity to attack their box. So I think we were very professional with good standards in the first half. Then, of course, the red card definitely helped us to finish - or to change - the structure of the game.

“In the second half we created plenty of chances. I wasn't happy that we weren't clinical and clean enough finishing these chances, because I think we dropped our level a little bit there. Overall, though, winning 4–0 means that we did a lot of things well.”

Here are the key dates for the 2026/27 UEFA Conference League knockout stages, should Brighton progress:

- Knockout play-off round: February 18 and 25, 2027.

- Final: June 2, 2027 – Beşiktaş Stadium, Istanbul, Turkey.

#1844. Raheem Sterling dodges prison for dangerously driving Lamborghini

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

#1843. Doncaster Rovers 2 Huddersfield Town 3: 10-man Terriers emphatically end their barren league streak at bogey venue

Certainly for the victor, if there happens to be one.

Do the business, put your feet up - well, sort of - with three points in the bag ahead of a long weekend and watch the rest of your divisional rivals sweat it out.

That was the hope for both Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their differing third-tier missions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The incentive for Rovers was moving out of the drop zone up to 18th, while Town’s ambition revolved around securing the win that would draw them level with leaders Stockport County at the right end of the table.

Huddersfield were the ones smiling as they finally made hay at league level at what had previously been a bogey ground.

The first ever visitors here back on New Year’s Day 2007 - the 20th anniversary is in a month’s time - Town had not so much as scored in any of their previous four visits at league level.

They emphatically put paid to that on a night when they played with a man light for around an hour. You didn’t really guess.

For the first 34 minutes, this game simply wasn’t a contest. There were 19 places between these two rivals ahead of kick-off and it showed as Town cruised into a 2-0 lead, courtesy of Cameron Humphreys’ first goal of the campaign and a 15th strike of a goal-laden season for Joe Taylor before Bali Mumba’s Donny demons resurfaced.

In the league fixture here in February, a panicking handball saw him concede a penalty in the game-breaking moment.

In the present, he was the guilty party again - towards the same goal. He hauled down Jamie Sterry, who got on the wrong side of him following Robbie Gotts’ spotter’s badge of a pass.

Booked earlier for a sliding challenge he couldn’t complain about, Mumba was dismissed for a second yellow card—his second dismissal of the season.

Isaac Hutchinson sent the underemployed Matt Young the wrong way to make it 2-1 and out of nowhere, we had a game on.

But Town, not Rovers, grabbed the all-important fourth goal.

Unconvincing at the back, the hosts erred for a third time and Ilias Bronkhurst fired in a soothing third.

Even without an extra player, it was Town who had the wit going forward as Rovers lacked penetration and quality. Given their defensive charity, it wasn’t a good mix and it's easy to see why they are where they are in the standings.

A stoppage-time goal from home captain Owen Bailey revived Rovers, but it was not enough. Nowhere near.

Rovers, without the ineligible Alfie May under the terms of his loan, handed a first start to loanee James Collins, now finally over his long-term knee injury.

It was a psychologically important night for the veteran striker, who was injured almost exactly a year to the day on December 2, 2025 - ironically against Town. It was his last start.

Collins, who turns 36 on Tuesday, was afforded an early birthday present in the process. Sterry also returned to the Rovers’ starting line-up following illness. Brandon Hanlan dropped to the bench, with Tom Nixon absent.

Joe Low and Fletcher - lined up from the off for Town, coming in for Ibane Bowat and Bojan Radulovic.

Ahead of the game, Martin Drury had spoken about Rovers’ set-piece threat, with Low’s promotion seemingly something to do with that.

A gulf in class saw Town stroll most of the first-half, aided by the meek defensive tendencies which Rovers had avoided five days earlier at Bradford City. It eventually changed.

The promotion of Ashley Fletcher, who had delivered a fine cameo in the Trophy game here in early autumn - looked the shrewdest of moves from Drury.

He teed up Humphreys for an easy low finish for Town’s opener on five minutes after Mumba’s cross caused initial consternation as Rovers prevaricated at the back terribly.

Town mixed play up impressively and afforded themselves plenty of control and possession.

Last-ditch defending from ex-Terriers man Matty Pearson blocked Bronkhorst’s goalbound effort. A similarly alert block from Jack Senior repeated the trick to deny Low.

Town’s second was not long in coming on 21 minutes with Rovers again spooked by Fletcher, who showed adept chest control and neat footballing skills to set up Taylor, who fired home a clinical low volley as Rovers again stood and watched.

A brief half-chant of 'We turn up, why don't you' arrived from disgruntled Rovers patrons in the Black Bank.

Mumba’s indiscretion changed the complexion of the night and Thomas spurned a chance to level before the break, planting a free header over.

Ahead of the resumption, Grant McCann threw on another attack-minded player in Hakeeb Adelakun. His side saw a lot of the ball in the opening part of the second period, but couldn’t conjure a big chance against 10-man Town.

It was the visitors, who still possessed the killer instinct.

Sanches Fernandes rattled the crossbar and from the resultant corner, Rovers’ defensive deficiencies again re-surfaced.

The ball found Bronkhorst and after his initial effort was blocked, he rammed home a low drive in front of the ecstatic 1,905 Terriers supporters.

Bailey ensured there was a nervy finale for the visitors, firing home from Adelakun's low cross. But it was Town's night, deservedly.

Doncaster Rovers: Simkin; Sterry, Grehan (Ayinde 70), Pearson, Senior, Thomas (Husband 84); Gotts, Bailey, Broadbent (Adelakun HT), Hutchinson (O’Reilly 65); J Collins (Hanlan 65). Substitutes unused: Clarke, Bryne. Huddersfield Town: Young; Balker, Low, Roughan; Bronkhorst, A Collins (Ledson 69), Humphreys, Mumba, Sanches Fernandes (Bowat 84), Taylor (Radulovic 84); Fletcher (Harness 55). Substitutes unused: Alnwick, Gooch, Ashia.

Attendance: 8,376 (1,905 Huddersfield Town supporters).
