#1797. GdS: Why Cisse’s position remains a dilemma despite continuous flow of goals

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

#1796. Thomas Frank identifies Crystal Palace ‘turning point’ as former Tottenham boss claims first win

Thomas Frank believes his first win as Crystal Palace manager can be a “turning point” in the club’s season.

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table but tasted victory for the first time in Frank’s tenure with a 2-1 win over 10-man Real Sociedad in his second game in charge.

The Eagles came from behind after trailing to a second-half goal by Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr.

But Jean-Philippe Mateta levelled from the penalty spot after Jon Martin was shown a second yellow card and sent off for the side sat fifth in La Liga.

Palace then scored their eventual winner through substitute Dwight McNeil but almost threw it away when Dean Henderson was required to make a last-gasp save after Yeremy Pino had seen the Eagles’ second spot-kick of the night saved.

Palace’s victory came five days after their 3-2 defeat at Coventry in Frank’s first match in charge.

“In the second half I felt we kept the ball much better,” Frank said after his side’s victory on Thursday.

“What I really liked was the belief from the players. It is so important to keep doing the right things and keep believing.”

Palace were guilty of giving the ball away in poor errors and handing Sociedad some cheap chances despite eventually closing out a victory.

Frank said: “We should just control that game. But we probably don’t have the confidence right now.

Asked whether the win against Sociedad can be a turning point in a so-far difficult season for the south Londoners, Frank replied: “I think it could be. But we need to follow it up, of course, with a good performance against Hull on Sunday. But there were a lot of positives from this game.”

Liverpool meanwhile make the short trip over to the Hill Dickinson Stadium for the first Merseyside derby of the season with Everton picking up just one win in their last 10 meetings with their neighbours.

As ever, England legend and Betfair ambassador Alan Shearer has revealed his Premier League predictions to Metro.

What a tough one to call. Big, big game for both clubs. Big game for both managers. We saw Forest when they went up against City, didn’t we? We thought, ‘Okay, maybe this is what we’re about to see in Liam Delap and that performance’. But then it went against them again last weekend.

Chelsea, I don’t know. I haven’t got a clue what’s going to happen because they just got battered into submission by Leeds and that would be the worry. I think this is such a tough one to call. #1793. Xabi Alonso hits back at Jamie Carragher criticism as ‘responsibility’ claimed for Chelsea defending

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso says he takes the “whole responsibility” for Chelsea’s dismal defending but disagrees with his friend Jamie Carragher that Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill will never be a good enough centre-back pairing for the Blues.

Fofana and Colwill were heavily criticised for their performances last Saturday as the west Londoners were thrashed 4-1 at home to Leeds in the Premier League.

The defeat exposed further weaknesses in Alonso’s defence and proved the worst possible response to their disappointing previous outing, the 1-0 defeat to Sunderland before the international break.

Chelsea head to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest on Friday night eager to get back to winning ways.

Analysing the Leeds loss, Carragher said on Sky Sports: “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League.”

Speaking about Fofana and Colwill, he added: “As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.”

Asked whether he had seen these comments from his former Liverpool team-mate, Alonso said he had not, before adding: “I must disagree. I disagree with Carra. For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good [against Leeds]. But I think I’ve seen them [Colwill and Fofana] play well, and I’ve seen them show good levels.

“This is the goal and the challenge – to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent.”

Alonso, speaking more broadly about Chelsea’s poor defending, added: “There are no excuses not to do better. We are in the process. Taking steps, taking a step forward but until it is totally in the DNA of the team it takes time.

“I take the whole responsibility of the team and how they perform. We need to show [improvement against Forest], not just talk. Talk is cheap. It’s about performing on the pitch.

“We want to be back on that more solid feeling that we had. This was hopefully one-[off], and we don’t want to repeat it.”

#1792. Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth: Cherries become third club to achieve rare feat with latest Europa League win

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 22:46, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:25

Bournemouth have become just the third team to win their first five main draw matches in a major European competition.

The Cherries travelled to Vigo with a perfect record in the competition after beating Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, AC Milan and Sparta Prague.

Their impressive record looked set to end when they went a goal and a man down inside the first quarter at Balaidos.

Bournemouth showed character to recover from Bafode Diakite's red card by staging a dramatic second-half turnaround that started with Alvaro Rodriguez's equaliser.

Rayan then netted a 78th-minute winner to fire the Cherries to a 2-1 victory, sending them into an outright lead at the top of the Europa League league phase with the only 100% record out of the 36 teams.

Not only have they significantly boosted their chances of securing a top-eight finish, but the Cherries also became the third team to win their first five main draw games in European competition.

German side Nurnberg were the first team to achieve the feat on their way to reaching the quarter-finals of the 1961-1962 European Cup.

Armenian side Ararat Yerevan replicated the feat when they won the first five games of their UEFA Cup campaign in 1972-1973 before losing on penalties to Kaiserslautern in the last 16.

As well as joining Nurnberg and Ararat in an exclusive group, Bournemouth also became the first Premier League side in three years to win a competitive game after trailing at half time while being a player down.

Prior to Thursday's win, Liverpool were the last team to achieve that feat when Darwin Nunez netted a late brace in a 2-1 victory after Virgil van Dijk had been sent off in the first period.

Another SPECIAL night ❤️ ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. Sturm Graz ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Sunderland ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. AC Milan ⭕️ W 0-3 vs. Man Utd ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. Aston Villa ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Leeds ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Sparta Prague ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Ipswich ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Nottingham Forest ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Celta Vigo THE SPIRIT IN THIS TEAM ???

After winning 10 consecutive games in all competitions for the first time in their history, Bournemouth will now start preparation for Sunday's Premier League meeting with Fulham at Craven Cottage.

Marco Rose's side will then play two more league games against Brighton & Hove Albion and Hull City before they return to Europa League action against Viktoria Plzen on December 10.

Bournemouth head into the weekend in fifth spot in the Premier League table and just three points adrift of fourth-placed Liverpool.

#1788. Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling new era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

The fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

His assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

There were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

He is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better

Liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

It helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

The German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

And that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

#1785. Arsenal, Man United and Aston Villa handed Joaquin Seys boost as defender makes transfer admission

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 22:49

Arsenal, Aston Villa and Manchester United have received a major boost in their pursuit of Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys, after the defender said he believes he is ready to move to a top club.

The 21-year-old Belgium international has become one of Europe's most promising full-backs since coming through the Belgian champions’ academy.

Reports suggest all three Premier League clubs watched Seys closely and made enquiries during the summer transfer window.

United saw him as a long-term answer to their left-back concerns, while Villa considered him a possible replacement for Lucas Digne.

Arsenal, meanwhile, could draw on the relationship established through the signing of Christos Tzolis.

Despite previously insisting he was solely focused on Club Brugge, Seys has now suggested to Het Laatste Nieuws that a high-profile departure could materialise at the end of the season.

"I believe you can go straight from here to a top club," Seys said via Sport Witness. "After all, with Club Brugge, we've already proven in the Champions League that we're on par with teams often viewed as 'stepping-stone' clubs. So, yes. I feel ready for it."

The defender added that any summer exit will depend entirely on the specific project on offer, stressing he would never leave Brugge simply for the sake of a transfer.

Addressing the summer interest from England, Seys reiterated that nothing became concrete enough to push for an exit and insisted he was perfectly content when Brugge opted to keep him.

The young wide defender has backed up his growing ambition on the pitch this term, registering four assists in 12 Belgian Pro League outings alongside a goal against Lens and two assists against PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Club Brugge have quickly emerged as a favoured target for England’s biggest clubs after impressing on the European stage.

Arsenal raided the Jan Breydel Stadium for winger Christos Tzolis over the summer and are now competing with Man United for prolific striker Nicolo Tresoldi.

Seys is contracted until June 2029, leaving the Belgian club in a strong position should a summer bidding war develop.

However, the eight-cap international's public declaration that he is ready to take the next step is set to alert Arsenal, Aston Villa and United as they prepare their recruitment plans for 2027.

#1782. Luka Vuskovic reveals new details on Tottenham exit and when he may leave Brighton

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Vuskovic joined Spurs in 2023 in a £12million deal from Croatian side Hajduk Split before being sent on loan to Radomiak Radom in Poland, Westerlo in Belgium and German outfit Hamburg.

During that time, Vuskovic developed a reputation as one of Europe’s brightest young defenders and was named in last year’s Bundesliga team of the season.

The 19-year-old, who was called up to Croatia’s World Cup squad over the summer, returned to Spurs at the end of last season but found his path to the first team blocked as Roberto De Zerbi’s side moved swiftly to sign centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

With Spurs unwilling to offer Vuskovic assurances over his playing time, they agreed a £52m deal with Brighton.

The move has paid off handsomely for Vuskovic, who has been a key part of Brighton’s stellar start to the season, with the Seagulls second in the Premier League, and he says he had decided his future early this summer.

“That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they said they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

“Tottenham said they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”

You want to be somewhere where you are stable, where you can spend a few years, where you can develop more

Vuskovic’s performances have prompted transfer links with the likes of Liverpool and fellow European giants, but the youngster is happy at Brighton for now.

Vuskovic never made a senior competitive appearance for Spurs and was out on loan as the club went from Europa League winners to relegation candidates in the space of 12 chaotic months.

During that period, Spurs went through four different managers, with Ange Postecoglu, Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor and De Zerbi all in the hot seat while Vuskovic watched from afar at Hamburg.

Despite being on the books at Spurs, Vuskovic’s future at the club was always up in the air, and he admits he never once got a call from any of the club’s managers to check on him when he was out on loan.

“I never spoke with any Tottenham coach. They never called me,” Vuskovic continued.

“I had one guy from Tottenham, Andy [Scoulding, Tottenham’s performance manager], he spent a lot of time calling me, asking if I need help, and also some physios if I ever needed anything, nutritionists also. But never from the coaches.”

#1780. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

#1778. Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he said as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

The 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the new manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

None of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a big defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United

The two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

But that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

There was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

But Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at big clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has said he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker showed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

He signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

Palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With big money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, currently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history

Of the new managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical issues stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

Lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a new contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

The fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

#1776. Hamburger SV vs Bayern Munich - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 23:19, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:12

Bayern Munich will hope to arrest their troubles by getting the better of hosts Hamburger SV at Volksparkstadion on Saturday and reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga table.

The Bavarians are second with 22 points in the league, so they will need Borussia Dortmund to avoid winning in order to climb to first, whereas the home side are 12th with 12 points.

Hamburger's campaign has been positive, especially as they have taken three more points after 10 matchweeks this season than they did at the same stage in 2025-26.

The club did lose 4-0 against Werder Bremen on November 22, and a defeat on the weekend could leave them just two points above the bottom three.

Head coach Daniel Thioune will be alarmed that his side have lost four of their last five games in all competitions, with the club scoring five goals while conceding on 12 occasions.

The Green-Whites' next task is to get the better of Bayern for the first time since July 2011, a period in which they suffered 17 defeats and drew three times.

HSV's record as hosts has been commendable this term considering they have triumphed in three of their five league outings at Volksparkstadion, though they were beaten twice in that stretch.

Bayern are in the unusual position of having to bounce back from a loss after Lille won 2-1 against them in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That was Vincent Kompany's second game on the touchline following his collapse in October, but his first match back was hardly better, with his side drawing 1-1 with FC Koln on November 20.

The visitors are only two points behind first-placed Borussia Dortmund, but with numerous injuries throughout the squad, there are fears that the gap could widen.

Injuries and form are not the only problems plaguing the champions, whose hierarchy have come under fire for their handling of Jamal Musiala's health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to speak up in support of the attacker.

Nevertheless, it should not be forgotten that the Bavarians have scored 30 goals in 10 top-flight games, while only Dortmund have conceded fewer goals than their 10.

Bayern's defeat against Lille was their first in any competition this campaign, and it was also their first away defeat, with the visitors having won six and drawn three of their first nine away fixtures of the season.

Hamburger midfielder Nicolai Remberg has been ruled out for the rest of the season, meaning the hosts may have to rely upon Nicolas Capaldo in the middle of the pitch.

With striker Yussuf Poulsen unavailable, Patson Daka will be expected to lead the line, and he may be supported by Fabio Vieira.

Bayern will be without Harry Kane for months due to an ankle injury, and to make matters worse, Michael Olise is a doubt.

Luis Diaz should be ready to feature in some capacity on the weekend, though he faces the prospect of playing in a forward line led by natural midfielder Konrad Laimer.

Aleksandar Pavlovic played in an advanced role against Lille due to injuries in attack, but he should be able to return to a deeper role alongside Kimmich.

Fernandes; Nandja, Bornauw, Omari; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Capaldo, Gronbaek, Wolfe; Daka, Vieira

Urbig; Stanisic, Upamecano, Tah, Ito; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Diaz, Karl, Brown; Laimer

Hamburger may never have a better opportunity than now to take points from Bayern, who have several key absentees.

However, Bayern still boast immense quality in their squad, and they should still be able to come out on top, even if the match is far from straightforward.

#1775. CM: Gimenez could terminate Porto loan early and return to Milan – the situation

Santiago Gimenez left AC Milan in the summer, but he may be returning before the end of his loan deal next summer.

It’s fair to say that Gimenez is one of the most difficult signings to assess from Milan in recent years. On paper, it made plenty of sense why he was right to arrive; he was firing in the Champions League, he had no difficulty scoring in the league and there was the added bonus of him being young and a fan of the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With goals against elite teams in Europe too, it made sense why he’d be able to have a successful career at San Siro. Performing on the biggest stage seemingly wasn’t an issue.

After almost being forced out of the club last summer, an injury-ridden campaign effectively ended his time with the Diavolo and he was loaned out in the summer. Yet, he could already be heading back to Italy.

As Calciomercato.com writes, it’s highly unlikely that Porto will activate the €18m buy clause in his deal, and it’s even possible that he doesn’t see out the complete spell of his loan. What is for sure, though, is that his value has only dropped further with his Portuguese adventure…

#1774. Man Utd have key edge in Nico Paz transfer talks as connection revealed

Manchester United have a potential ace up their sleeve in transfer talks over Nico Paz.

Argentine star Paz is enjoying a burgeoning reputation across Europe after a remarkable start to the season with Como, which has seen him score six goals from attacking midfield - including two against Man Utd in the Champions League last month.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not currently favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is said to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Athletic also report that Pochettino, a fellow Argentine, shares agents with Paz, which could make transfer negotiations easier for all parties.

Man Utd are keen on the player and 22-year-old's agency connection to their head coach potentially a factor in any pursuit.

One sticking point is that Paz is likely to want to play in the Champions League, so qualification this season may prove key to his final destination.

Man Utd's interest comes amid uncertainty over Fernandes, who recently confirmed talks over a contract extension have been put on hold due to the club’s ongoing poor results.

Fernandes’s current deal runs until the end of the 2026-27 season, although Man Utd retain the option to extend it by a further year.

Paz is among the options being considered as Man Utd weigh up the possibility of Fernandes departing, but competition for the midfielder is expected to be fierce and the club are also assessing alternative targets.

#1773. SBV Excelsior vs Telstar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 26 Nov 2026 23:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:10

SBV Excelsior host SC Telstar at Stadion Woudestein in Rotterdam in round 14 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday with kick-off at 3.30pm GMT.

Excelsior and Telstar drew 2-2 at BUKO Stadion on November 1, 2025 and again at Stadion Woudestein on January 17, 2026, but the Kralingers now sit 13th on 14 points, four clear of the relegation play-off place that De Witte Leeuwen occupy on 10.

Ruben den Uil's Excelsior ended a run of five straight league defeats with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on November 21, their first league victory at De Kuip since 1980.

After Givairo Read gave Feyenoord a lead on two minutes, Mario Dominguez levelled on six, Irakli Yegoian scored a penalty on 40 and Casper Widell headed in from a corner on 58.

Jan Plug, who is on loan from Feyenoord, turned the ball into his own net on 67 minutes, but the visitors held on.

Excelsior had 10 points from their first five games, including a 4-0 win at Cambuur on the opening day, then took one point from the next seven.

The low point came on November 1, when Twente won 9-0 at Woudestein, the heaviest league defeat in the club's history, with Nesto Groen sent off after five minutes.

A 1-0 home loss to Go Ahead Eagles on November 7 left Excelsior without a league goal in four games, and they had conceded 20 times in five league matches before the Feyenoord win, leaving a goal difference of -12 from 13 games.

Henk Brugge, in his first permanent head coach job after succeeding Anthony Correia in May, has Telstar 16th on the Eredivisie table with 10 points from two wins, four draws and seven defeats, with 19 goals scored and 28 conceded.

Telstar went ahead after 16 minutes against PEC Zwolle on November 21 through a Simon Graves own goal, but Dylan Mbayo scored twice before half time and Ibrahim Cissoko added a third after a poor back pass from Gabi Caschili.

That 3-1 home defeat means Telstar have gone 17 matches without beating Zwolle in all competitions, and Brugge admitted afterwards that his side may have played the better football but defended badly at key moments.

Telstar have scored in each of their last six league games, 14 goals in all, but they conceded 16 across those matches, including a 4-2 win over Utrecht and 2-2 draws with ADO Den Haag and at Fortuna Sittard.

The defence is the problem at BUKO Stadion, where Telstar have conceded 20 goals in seven league games this season.

Away from Velsen-Zuid, Telstar have taken one point from their last three league trips, losing 1-0 at AZ Alkmaar and 3-2 at Go Ahead Eagles before the 2-2 draw at Fortuna Sittard, and Tyrone Owusu leads the team with five goals this season.

Excelsior have no reported injuries or suspensions, with Groen available again after serving his ban by missing the Go Ahead Eagles game and the trip to Feyenoord.

Sliti, who has three league goals, feared a bruised or broken thumb after Netherlands Under-21s duty on November 17 but started at De Kuip, so Alireza Jahanbakhsh and David Garden remain options from the bench.

Noah Naujoks is back in the midfield after a long injury absence and started alongside Lennard Hartjes, who has suffered three cruciate ligament tears in his career, two of them at Excelsior.

Telstar have no confirmed absentees, with Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes both returning from injury as substitutes against Zwolle, on 57 and 84 minutes respectively.

Nokkvi Thorisson and Jeff Hardeveld, who both came on after 57 minutes against Zwolle, are options to start in attack.

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Naujoks, Hartjes, Yegoian; Sliti, Dominguez, Thorsteinsson

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Martha, Owusu, Demircan; Brouwer

Excelsior showed at Feyenoord that the goals have returned, with a side that had scored once in five league games finding the net three times against the division's second-highest scoring attack, including a Widell header from a corner and a Dominguez finish after a midfield giveaway.

Telstar have scored in six straight league games, so a clean sheet is unlikely for an Excelsior defence that has conceded 31 times in 13 matches, but Telstar have taken one point from their last three away games and let in 20 goals in seven home league games, which suggests their backline will struggle with Dominguez and Sliti.

The counter-argument is the 9-0 Twente result, yet that came with Groen sent off after five minutes, while the draws in both meetings last season show Telstar can score at Woudestein, so Excelsior should edge a match in which both sides concede.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Pep Chavarria has urged his Chelsea team-mates to “give a lot more” against Nottingham Forest than they did in last weekend’s dire defeat by Leeds.

Transfer news LIVE: Paz to Arsenal twist; Man Utd boost; Chelsea shock

Chelsea XI vs Nottingham Forest: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

How to watch Nottm Forest vs Chelsea: TV channel and live stream

The Blues head to the City Ground on Friday night looking to get back to winning ways after successive Premier League losses, with a 4-1 home thrashing by their old rivals following a 1-0 defeat at struggling Sunderland prior to the international break.

Xabi Alonso’s side have been criticised for their poor defending and a perceived lack of intensity in recent performances, and summer signing Chavarria is keen for them to put that right against a Forest team that currently sit nine places below them in the table.

“We have to give a lot more because, in the end, we’re at a club where the demands are at a different level,” he told Chelsea’s official media channels.

“We know the responsibility we have and I think we’ve realised that we can’t repeat a match like that [the Leeds game] again.

“Obviously, on any given day we can win, we can lose, or we can draw, but the attitude we had, I think, wasn’t right, and we players know that it was our fault. So we’re already mentally focused on going all out with the bit between our teeth.

“We’re going to treat Nottingham Forest like it’s the last game we play, and we truly believe it, we take it seriously. That’s the only way, because football now is so competitive that any team can beat you.

“Ultimately, it will be a hard-fought match with a lot of individual duels, decided by small details, like most games are. We have to stay extremely focused so that we land the first blow.”

Discussing his own performances, the 28-year-old added: “I’m trying to give my absolute best. I know I can give a lot more. I think in these matches that progression is going to show.”

Published: 18:28 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:19 EST, 23 November 2026

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

Neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'

Emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

An interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he said: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club

'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'

It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.

#1770. FC Koln vs Elversberg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 26 Nov 2026 23:26

FC Koln will be looking to end their five-game winless run in the Bundesliga when they welcome newly promoted Elversberg to the RheinEnergieStadion on Saturday afternoon.

The Billy Goats will take confidence from their impressive draw against Bayern Munich, while the visitors arrive having lost five of their last seven matches across all competitions.

Several sides above them in the table have suffered more defeats, but Koln’s joint-high number of draws has prevented them from making a serious push up the Bundesliga standings.

However, their 1-1 draw away to Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena last Friday night was certainly one point worth celebrating.

The Billy Goats ended their six-match losing run against the bruised German champions, and allowed Borussia Dortmund to reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga.

Buoyed by that performance, Koln will now be targeting their first league victory since early October, which would bring an end to their five-game winless run in the competition.

The hosts will be further encouraged by the fact they won three of their six home games across all competitions this season, scoring 12 goals along the way.

Since collecting seven points from their opening four Bundesliga matches, Elversberg have begun to discover just how difficult life in Germany’s top flight can be.

Representing a town with a population of around 13,000, the newly promoted side were always likely to face an uphill battle against German football’s biggest clubs.

Their recent form has underlined the scale of that challenge, with Elversberg suffering five defeats in their last seven matches across all competitions.

On a slight positive note, all but one of those losses have come by a single-goal margin - a stat which shows just how competitive the Black and Whites have been.

That narrow pattern continued in their most recent games, as Vincent Wagner’s side endured a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund before losing 1-0 to Freiburg last Saturday.

Despite that latest setback, Wagner believes his men delivered their best defensive performance of the season, restricting Freiburg to just one shot on target.

Results may have dipped, but the supporters have continued to show their backing, with around 5,000 expected to make the trip to Cologne - almost 40% of the entire population of the town.

Meanwhile, Wagner has already hinted that the club could explore the January transfer market, with sporting director Christian Weber understood to have a recruitment plan in mind.

Koln have one or two selection concerns heading into Saturday’s clash, mainly regarding the availability of Ragnar Ache.

The 28-year-old has been sidelined with a thigh injury since the start of October and, despite returning to training five weeks ago, is yet to make an appearance.

Head coach Wagner described Ache as “fit, training and eager”, although his lack of match action continues to leave a big question mark around his name.

Fellow striker Thijs Dallinga is a more definite absentee, having been ruled out for the remainder of the season with a torn cruciate ligament.

This means that Wagner could turn to either Marius Bulter or Malek El Mala to lead the attacking efforts alongside Said El Mala.

There are also concerns over captain and goalkeeper Marvin Schwabe, who landed awkwardly during last Friday’s draw with Bayern Munich and missed training on Monday and Tuesday due to back pain.

Veteran keeper Ron-Robert Zieler could replace him, though it is worth noting that the 2014 World Cup winner has not tasted competitive action in a little over 12 months.

When it comes to Elversberg, the visitors are almost injury-free, with the exception of Nicholas Mickelson, who returned from international duty with a knee problem.

There are also slight doubts over the availability of Lasse Gunther and Nicolas Kristof, who are both struggling with colds.

Noah Darvich, who is suffering from muscular problems, is a doubt and a decision over his availability could be made as late as Saturday morning.

Zieler; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Okon-Engstler, Sosa; Maina, Moore; Bulter, S. El Mala

Kristof; Gyamerah, Pinckert, Rohr, Gunther; Keidel, Poreba; Petkov, Onyeka, Krattenmacher; Mokwa

Everything points to a close game in Cologne, with the hosts performing well on home soil and the visitors seeing most of their games determined by single-goal margins.

Koln will be buoyed by their result against Bayern Munich and we are backing their momentum to continue with a narrow win over a plucky and dangerous Elversberg side.

#1769. Manchester United confirm Bruno Fernandes absence ahead of Brentford clash

Bruno Fernandes has emerged as a key fitness doubt for Manchester United’s Premier League clash with Brentford this weekend.

United have confirmed that their influential captain missed Friday morning’s training session at Carrington as a precaution due to feeling unwell and will need to be assessed ahead of Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge at Old Trafford on Saturday.

A late decision is expected to be made on his availability for that game, with ESPN reporting that Harry Maguire is expected to be in contention to face Brentford after reporting an unspecified injury in the aftermath of Wednesday night’s chaotic 2-2 draw against Sporting in the Champions League.

Pochettino will be expected to give an update on both players when he addresses the media at Carrington in his pre-Brentford press conference at 1:30pm GMT on Friday afternoon.

“Manchester United have trained in front of the cameras in the Carrington rain on Friday morning,” United said via their official media channels.

“Mauricio Pochettino's side are preparing for Saturday's 15:00 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford, our head coach's first home game in charge.

“Bruno Fernandes was absent from the session, after scoring both goals in the 2-2 draw against his former club Sporting in the UEFA Champions League in midweek.

“The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”

The absence of Fernandes would be a significant blow for Pochettino as he seeks to achieve his first win as United boss at the third attempt, having overseen a 4-0 drubbing by arch-rivals Liverpool in his opening match at the helm at Anfield last weekend.

Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes to set the tone for that one-sided contest on Merseyside, but has since seen his red card for a last-man challenge on Alexander Isak overturned by a Football Association (FA) regulatory commission following a successful appeal in a ruling that has caused plenty of controversy.

#1767. Alejandro Garnacho threatening to become a problem again for Chelsea

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea are facing a potential problem surrounding Alejandro Garnacho.

The Argentine, firmly out of favour at Stamford Bridge, joined Aston Villa in the summer on a loan deal which included a conditional obligation to make the move permanent for £42.5million at the end of the season.

While the conditions that would trigger Garnacho’s permanent exit remain undisclosed, they are believed to involve the player making a certain number of appearances which Chelsea sources described at the time as easily achievable. Villa are also paying a loan fee.

However, with Garnacho being left out of four of Villa’s last five matchday squads, there is now growing doubt over whether the 22-year-old’s Chelsea exit will become permanent.

Chelsea placed a public valuation of £43m on Garnacho in July once the club’s hierarchy decided they wanted to sell him.

Garnacho’s initial preference had been to move overseas, and there was interest from Saudi Arabia, Serie A and elsewhere in Europe, until Villa made their interest known, shortly after selling their best player, Morgan Rogers, to Chelsea for £117m.

Garnacho has featured in just seven of Villa’s 19 games across all competitions so far this season, and is yet to start for Unai Emery’s side.

Garnacho’s exile continued this week in the Champions League clash at Galatasaray, where Emery decided to name just 11 out of a possible 12 substitutes - two of which were goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s latest absence, Emery said: “The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.”

The Athletic have since reported that Villa are exploring their options to get rid of the player in January, though it remains to be seen if Chelsea would welcome such talks.

Chelsea and Villa could jointly agree to terminate the loan agreement, which would allow Garnacho to explore options elsewhere. But that would require both clubs agreeing to do so, and the chances of Chelsea getting a fee similar to the £42.5m Villa had committed to again appear slim.

The situation is threatening to become a headache which Chelsea believed they had remedied.

Chelsea may instead point to the chance that Garnacho’s minutes improve in the second half of the campaign as reason to keep the Argentine in situ.

#1766. Dundee United vs St Johnstone - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 04:03

Hoping to create some separation in the top half of the Scottish Premiership table, Dundee United will welcome St Johnstone to Tannadice Park on Saturday.

The Tangerines could make it nine games unbeaten this weekend, while the Saints are keen to bounce back from defeat last time out.

Jim Goodwin's Dundee Utd have proven immensely resilient this term, and arrive full of confidence having lost just once on home turf in the league.

Adding to that feeling is the fact the Tangerines thrashed Hibernian 4-0 on the road last Saturday, thanks to a brace from Zachary Sapsford and second-half efforts from Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall.

That victory has Goodwin's side fifth in the Scottish Premiership table with 20 points from their 13 matches, a tally that sees them three clear of city rivals Dundee in seventh having played one game fewer.

United will be aiming to distance themselves from the bottom half this weekend, though it is notable they have drawn as many matches as they have won in 2026-27, including three of their last five.

The hosts also kept just one clean sheet during that spell while conceding six goals in the process, letting in two in the 3-2 home win over Aberdeen, and two in the 2-2 stalemate at Celtic on October 28.

Meanwhile, Simo Valakari's St Johnstone are feeling the pressure from their rivals, and face a tough test to stay in the top half this weekend.

The Saints were downed 2-1 by Falkirk last Saturday, falling two goals behind shortly after the interval and only pulling one back late on through Josh Campbell.

That defeat brought a three-game unbeaten streak to an end, and means that Valakari's side arrive having triumphed in just one of their last six matches, beating Dundee 2-1 on November 7.

To make matters worse, St Johnstone failed to keep a clean sheet in any of those six clashes, conceding two or more on four separate occasions.

Currently sixth with 17 points after 14 games, the Saints will be looking over their shoulder given they are level with Dundee and just three points ahead of Aberdeen, Hibernian and 10th-placed St Mirren.

Knowing that they are at risk of dropping down into the bottom six, fans of the visitors will also be concerned after seeing their team score the fewest goals of any team in the top half (18).

Dundee Utd will be without attacker Neil Farrugia due to a groin injury, while versatile left-back Will Ferry is dealing with a muscle issue.

In their absence, Jesse Randall and Daniel Bennie look set to support striker Zachary Sapsford up top on Saturday, with Joshua Rawlins and Kevin Ciubotaru offering further width from full-back.

As for St Johnstone, they are missing centre-back Morgan Boyes, who has a calf injury to contend with, though Danny Finlayson and Bozo Mikulic should be on hand to start at the heart of the visitors' defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, winger Unax Alvarez has a calf injury of his own, and attacking midfielder Jamie Gullan is sidelined due to a groin problem.

With that in mind, Josh Fowler should lead the line this weekend, flanked by Taylor Steven and Kai Fotheringham.

Walton; Rawlins, Esselink, Forbes, Ciubotaru; Cameron, Tait, Iqbal; Randall, Sapsford, Bennie

Steward; Smith, Finlayson, Mikulic, Alic; Cotterill, Holt, Campbell; Steven, Fowler, Fotheringham

Dundee United have been commendably resilient in recent weeks, though their ability to get wins over the line on a consistent basis has been lacking.

However, St Johnstone will be feeling the pressure from their rivals this weekend, and after failing to keep a clean sheet in their last six matches, the visitors' leaky defence could see them lose once again on Saturday.

#1765. Thomas Frank sends warning to Yeremy Pino over Crystal Palace issue

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has called on Yeremy Pino to improve his disciplinary record.

The Spanish attacker has been one of Palace’s better players in a difficult season, but is suspended for Sunday’s clash with Hull after picking up his fifth yellow card of the Premier League season in last weekend’s 3-2 defeat at Coventry.

Pino was also booked in Thursday’s 2-1 Europa League win over 10-man Real Sociedad, and Frank admitted discipline was something the 24-year-old would have to work on.

“Yes, I think it’s fair to say,” Frank said. “I think he’s a very good player — very important for us and has gone up a level this season — so of course it is disappointing.

“It is something he needs to work on. That is too many yellow cards. Of course, we would have loved to play with Yeremy and [Ismaila] Sarr and JP [Jean-Philippe Mateta] in an important match — three of our best offensive players — but others will need to step up and show what they can do.”

Asked whether Palace had picked up any new knocks against Sociedad, Frank replied: “Not that I am aware of, so hopefully not.”

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table and have half the tally of 14 points 11th-place Hull have taken from their first 11 games.

“It will be difficult against a Hull team that is fighting with every inch of their bodies from all players on the pitch,” Frank said.

#1763. Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapses during post-match interview as journalist tries to break his fall after he 'felt dizzy' at the end of the first half of Boca Juniors' cup glory

Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026

Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors

The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf

'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'

Fortunately, Paredes was revived quickly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in New York at the World Cup final in July.

Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'

Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades)

'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'

Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'

#1761. Toulouse vs Rennes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 01:56

Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.

Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.

For the second time domestically this season, Toulouse failed to emerge victorious last week when scoring first.

Those four points dropped represent the difference between their current position and a spot in Europe next season.

On the other hand, they have avoided defeat in seven of their last eight league games, including the last three at Stadium de Toulouse.

In their last three Ligue 1 home contests, this team have netted a combined six goals, six more than in their opening two games played in Toulouse.

Discipline has been an issue for Jens Berthel Askou’s men in the top flight this season, as they average the second-most fouls per match in the competition (15.7).

Toulouse can extend their Ligue 1 home unbeaten run versus Rennes on Sunday to five matches, last beating them in Toulouse in 2025 (2-1).

A campaign that began with so much promise has deteriorated for Stade Rennais, who have struggled to find consistency this month.

Franck Haise’s men are on a five-match winless run across all competitions, having begun 2026-27 unbeaten in their first five competitive fixtures.

A 3-1 loss at NEC in Europa League action on Thursday has them narrowly above the knockout stage line in that competition.

In November, they have netted a goal or fewer in each of their competitive games, while conceding a combined six times in their last three competitive outings.

Away from home, Rennes have really been exposed defensively in the league, conceding a combined 14 goals in their last four domestic matches as the visitors.

Les Rouge et Noirs are second in the league regarding expected goals, though they have conceded more penalties than anyone in the competition so far (five).

Toulouse may be without Mark McKenzie, who suffered a hamstring strain in their last match, while Aron Donnum is eligible to return from his suspension.

Jacen Russell-Rowe netted for them in the opening half at Lens, his third of the Ligue 1 campaign, tied with Thomas Jorgensen for second on the team.

A minor knock has Valentin Rongier questionable in this outing for Rennes, while Adrien Thomasson will miss the match with a red-card suspension.

Boulaye Dia scored in their draw at arch-rivals Lorient last Sunday, putting him up to six in the league this season, one fewer than last season’s leading goalscorer in Ligue 1, Esteban Lepaul.

As much as they have struggled of late, we believe Rennes' firepower will be sharper this weekend and punish a Toulouse backline that is far from reassuring defensively.

#1760. Musiala sidelined ‘until further notice’ with hamstring injury

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jamal Musiala will be "out of action until further notice" after suffering a hamstring injury, Bayern Munich have confirmed.

Musiala has been restricted to just six appearances in all competitions this season, only two of which have been starts, due to a variety of issues.

In August, he revealed he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures" after collapsing twice on the pitch, during friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig.

Musiala did not return to action until September, but he subsequently suffered a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh while on international duty with Germany and returned to his club early.

The attacking midfielder has made back-to-back substitute appearances in Bayern's last two games – a 1-1 draw with Koln and a 2-1 defeat to Lille – but he now faces another stint on the sidelines.

A statement issued by the club on social media said: "FC Bayern's medical team have confirmed on Friday that Jamal Musiala has sustained a muscular injury in his right hamstring and will therefore be out of action until further notice.

Jamal Musiala sustains muscular injury. FC Bayern’s medical team have confirmed on Friday that Jamal Musiala has sustained a muscular injury in his right hamstring and will therefore be out of action until further notice. Get well soon, Jamal!  https://t.co/2OdwIPz0nF

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 27, 2026

Musiala also saw his 2025-26 campaign blighted by injury, making just 12 starts in all competitions after breaking his leg during Bayern's quarter-final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain at the 2025 Club World Cup.

Bayern were already without Harry Kane, Ismael Saibari, Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry and Alphonso Davies due to injury, though the latter trio are not viewed as long-term issues, with Gnabry and Davies returning to training on Friday.

#1759. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta reveals David Raya injury hope for crunch Man City clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta is hoping that David Raya will be fit to play for Arsenal against Manchester City on Sunday.

The Spanish goalkeeper is in a race against time to recover from the shoulder injury he picked up against Newcastle last weekend.

Raya watched from the stands in midweek as Arsenal drew at home to Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, with deputy and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga filling in over Illan Meslier.

Scans showed that Raya's injury was not a serious one, despite initial fears, and there are still hopes that he could hand Arsenal a major boost by being ready to start in the high-profile clash with City.

Asked at Friday’s pre-match press conference about Raya's availability, Arteta was keeping his cards close to his chest.

“I don’t know,” he said. “We still have a few hours before the game. We’re just trying to get everybody back.”

Asked if he hoped that Raya would be ready to face City, Arteta replied: “Yeah.”

Pressed on whether the goalkeeper was training, the Arsenal boss added: “Yeah. They’re all training. Bukayo [Saka] as well is training,” alluding to the individual work the winger is doing away from the main group.

If Raya is not fit, then Kepa will be expected to continue in goal for Arsenal, having deputised without any major issues on Tuesday.

It would be Kepa's first appearance against City since the Carabao Cup final last season, when he started at Wembley and endured a painful afternoon.

The former Chelsea stopper - who remains the most-expensive goalkeeper in football history - was booked after charging out of goal and bringing down Jeremy Doku, before spilling a cross right at Nico O'Reilly's feet to gift City the opener in their 2-0 win.

However, Arteta insisted that match would not be on Kepa’s mind if he was called into action.

“The experience that Kepa has is already incredible,” Arteta said.

“Just look at the teams he’s been involved [in], the squads that he’s been involved [in], the trophies that he’s won. There is none of that.”

#1758. Liverpool handed major boost as new three-man injury update revealed

Victor Munoz has avoided serious injury in a boost for Liverpool, who will likely remain without both Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch for Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton.

The Reds were handed a fresh fitness scare on Wednesday night as summer signing Munoz limped off shortly before half-time in their 3-0 away win over Club Brugge in the Champions League.

The Spanish winger was hurt after a strong challenge that came at the end of a brilliant run and received treatment on the pitch before going off and being replaced by Rio Ngumoha.

Any fears over a long-term lay-off have now been allayed, however, with Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola revealing that Munoz could return to training as soon as Saturday.

“With Victor, I think the good news is that after assessing him, there is no disruption in the knee, everything is fine,” Iraola said at his pre-Everton press conference on Friday. “But he has a big knock. It’s a big knock.

“He hasn’t trained today but he wants to try tomorrow. We’ll see how the bruise is. But I cannot tell you right now.”

Liverpool will definitely still be missing Gakpo against Everton, with the Netherlands forward set to sit out the third match in a row with a calf injury sustained on international duty.

“Cody definitely not [available against Everton],” Iraola said. “It’s a muscle injury so we have to wait a little bit until the process goes on and it heals.

“This kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last [Netherlands] game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline.

“But normally I don’t like to say timelines with injuries because every injury is different and some of them go quicker than others.

“It wasn’t a big injury but there is something there and you have to give the time to heal.”

Gakpo’s Dutch team-mate Gravenberch also seems unlikely to return for Liverpool against Everton as he continues to deal with heel pain, having not played at all for club or country since the Carabao Cup last-16 win over Chelsea a month ago.

“It’s going to be difficult,” Iraola said of the chances of the midfielder being available for Sunday’s short trip to the Hill Dickinson Stadium. “I cannot say no because these kinds of injuries are difficult.

“They don’t look like a big thing but you have the pain, it doesn’t go. Sometimes it’s better, you don’t know why. The next day, you come and it’s worse. He is dealing with this situation, we are trying to help him.

“The important thing is when he comes back he comes with no pain so he can play as free as possible.”
